findings.claim_defeated: 'No session, transcript or environment is consulted, so a second participant reproduces the reading from the artifact; it reads the working tree and not a git object, so that reproduction needs a clean tree, which is why every reading of this member has been taken at a frozen commit.'
findings.observed: A clean tree at a frozen commit is not sufficient and the environment is consulted. One of the three settled member addresses, services/observation, is a directory, and digest() walks it with rglob and folds in every file it finds. Python bytecode caches are gitignored, so they are invisible to git status and they are inside the digest. Two detached worktrees at 3ffa1b5, both reporting git status --porcelain with 0 lines, both with git rev-parse HEAD:services/observation at 44b94e528fadd70ea35c37f67edfa44c88b4b518, produced different candidate identities: proposal:recurrence/0ac0bc3810b6164b in the one where I had run python scripts/verify.py, and proposal:recurrence/785cd7eea6b17d50 in the one where I had not. Deleting the two __pycache__ directories under services/observation moved the first tree back to 785cd7eea6b17d50. The trigger is the repository's own required command: running verify.py, which the landing gate runs, changes the candidate identity of the member being landed. A third checkout gave a third value. The shared checkout at the same commit, git status --porcelain 0 lines, reads proposal:recurrence/7b7ca24c4d381c5b. Three clean checkouts of one commit, three candidate identities. The mechanism is that a CPython .pyc embeds the source file's modification time and size, so the bytes under a __pycache__ directory differ between any two checkouts that have imported the module, and services/observation is digested by rglob over every file under it. The identity is therefore not merely order-dependent within a checkout; it is very nearly unique per checkout.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the witnessing-method defect, not a code style point. A second participant is told it can reproduce the reading from the artifact at a frozen commit with a clean tree, and it cannot: the answer depends on whether anything has imported the observation service in that checkout. It is already a live trap. pass6.json and pass7.json both cite proposal:recurrence/785cd7eea6b17d50 as observed, and pass 7 reasons explicitly that 'neither side touched any of the three basis addresses, so the live proposal id is unchanged at 785cd7eea6b17d50'. A tenth reader who follows AGENTS.md and runs verify.py before measuring will read 0ac0bc3810b6164b and conclude those two shipped records are false. It also defeats the sixth witness's repair by aiming it at the wrong thing: that reading found an uncommitted byte moving the identity and the fix recorded was 'reproduction needs a clean tree', which does not reach ignored files. verify.py, lint.py and selfcheck are all unaffected, because selfcheck runs against a temporary fixture root and the live half deliberately pins no verdict, so this is not a false green. It is a false claim about reproducibility in a governed file plus an instrument whose output is not a function of its subject.
findings.how_derived: PLANT 14. Created two detached worktrees at 3ffa1b5, ran verify.py in one only, then ran sov_recurrence.py run in each three times; each tree was internally deterministic and the two disagreed. Called experience.gather() directly on both roots and diffed the source digests: scripts/sov_fresh.py and scripts/sov_reuse.py matched, services/observation did not, at ba84792b8c8a1bae against dfbb7b7ebd2dc64a. git status --porcelain --ignored named the two __pycache__ directories; removing them restored the digest. Then ran the same command in the shared checkout, which had imported the module during verification, and read a third distinct proposal id.
findings.repair_shape_if_wanted: Not mine to build and not to be filed elsewhere. The narrow fix is for digest()'s directory branch to skip what the repository already declares as not its bytes, and to say in the docstring what is excluded and why. The honest alternative is to say in the note that the identity is a function of the working tree including ignored files, so it is reproducible only from a fresh checkout. Either way the sentence 'no environment is consulted' needs to stop being there, and pass 6 and pass 7's cited digest needs a note saying which of the two it is.

verdict: REPRODUCED with dissent on four sentences and one instrument property. Every command claim reproduces exactly. The code repairs for P8-F3 and P8-F2 hold in the directions their findings named, and P8-F5 is repaired unclaimed. I dissent from three sentences the delta writes into contracts/custodies/phase-1-5.json - that narrowing the rule alone fails the self-check, that passes 7 and 8 would both refuse WITNESSED, and that an independence block is the only record of a container - and from one line in the pass-8 record it ships, that identity read below the document root is caught by a unit test. Separately I dissent from the note's standing claim that no environment is consulted and that a clean tree at a frozen commit makes the reading reproducible: it does not, and the candidate identity moves when the repository's own required verification command is run first. Landing at BUILT is supported and I found nothing that makes it wrong.
standing_supported: NONE. This observation supports no standing transition. The member stays BUILT at work_state PRESENTED, and the refusal of BUILT -> WITNESSED recorded by passes 1 through 8 is untouched by this reading and was not reopened by it, as directed. This record supports landing the branch with the member at that standing, which is a different act, takes no standing and is not an acceptance. Under grant:standing-landing-loop the landing needs verify PASS, lint PASS and an observation from a participant that did not build the change; I did not build it, both commands pass at exit 0 at 3ffa1b5, and this record is that observation for the landing and is not one for the standing.
judgement_items: None of the eight findings is judgement-typed. All eight are repairable inside this concern by the participant that holds it, at effect class RECORD_LOCAL, and none should be filed elsewhere. Doing so would move the defect out of the concern that owns it.

For the root seat, not asked and not blocking: whether an exit clause member may land at BUILT after nine readings that all declined to advance it, when eight of the nine ran inside the builder's container and model family. The repository cannot settle how independent they are and the note now says so.

Also not asked, and carried forward from pass 8 because this reading did not resolve it: whether a defeating fixture anchored to the rule it grades by an equality assertion satisfies the AGENTS.md requirement for a case proving the required refusal, or whether the anchor has to be independent of the rule. That is a question about the standard, not about this code.

Raised by P9-F5 and new here: whether a derived identity that a repository's own required verification command changes is fit to be cited as observed evidence in a record. Two shipped records cite a value that the ordinary workflow does not reproduce. That is a repair for the builder, and if the answer is that the identity should be a function of the committed artifact rather than the working tree, that is a question about what the instrument is for and it belongs to a seat, not to me.
